subject: Weekly leadership signalcheck — QBR readiness, OKR highlights, immediate asks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Weekly leadership signalcheck — QBR readiness, OKR highlights, immediate asks

Team —

Quick weekly signalcheck ahead of Monday's QBR dry run. I kept this tight; bold items are asks that need a decision or owner this week.

Wins (OKR progress)
- Inference throughput: Dedicated pools hit 1.15x baseline after the kernel tuning (team estimate: ~14% cost reduction on read-heavy workloads). Landing page and benchmark snippets ready for slides.
- Evals infra: new suite caught a prompt-regression in the L2 rerank model; rollback prevented a wider customer impact.
- Customer health: ACME pilot remains green; engagement metric up 22% w/ dedicated throughput.

Risks / Watchlist
- Latency regression on long-sequence requests (p95 +18% last 48h). Root-cause hypothesis: new batching heuristic + rare KV-cache eviction pattern on 80-token prefixes. Impact: intermittent media-generation pipelines and one integration test failing in staging. See attachments (latency-regression-samples.csv) and INF-9823.
- QBR slide gap: we still need one concise slide that connects the unit-economics gains to the 2027 capacity plan. Marketing needs that by EOD Friday to finalize the executive pack.
- Headcount ask in Platform SRE (2 ICs) is in hiring queue but will not surface before the QBR unless we fast-track approval.

Asks (action items / owners)
- (Action) Markus/Platform: confirm whether kernel tuning can be throttled for the long-sequence path or if we should patch the batching heuristic by tomorrow EOD. Impact: if not resolved, propose temporary rollout freeze for long-sequence routing.
- (Action) Laura: approve a 1-slide financial tie-in (I dropped a draft in Drive). Marketing will merge into the final deck.
- (Action) Vivek: recommend whether we grant a temporary credit (up to $25k) to ACME because they hit the regression during onboarding; sales is asking for a quick answer.
- (Action) Tessa/Jonas: finalize the runbook summary for the QBR handoff (we need an operations blurb and 2 escalation examples).

Meeting asks: if owners can confirm in thread (or ping me on Slack) by 5pm PT today I will fold into the dry-run deck.

Attachments: QBR-readiness-appendix.pdf (slides draft), latency-regression-samples.csv (traces & p95 samples), action-item-tracker.xlsx (live tracker).

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-09T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership signalcheck — QBR readiness, OKR highlights, immediate asks

Thanks, Soojin — useful and concise. A few quick notes: 

- Laura (ack): I'm happy to approve the financial slide draft but want to review the assumptions on the cost reduction before sign-off. I'll pull up the Drive doc now and leave comments by noon PT.
- Credits: please don't hand out credits without Sales & Finance alignment. Vivek, can you coordinate with Kelly in Finance? If we approve anything, let's scope it as a one-time onboarding credit tied to observed impact.
- Headcount: let's not fast-track hiring before we evaluate short-term mitigations (e.g., contractor/top-up) — Soojin, can you add a short mitigation column in the tracker for each hire request?

On the latency regression: make sure we have the story for the QBR that explains the root cause hypothesis and the mitigation. If we cannot show a mitigation timeline today, we should include a proposed rollback option in the runbook slide.

I'll be available for a 20m sync at 3:30pm PT if you want to run through the deck bullet-by-bullet.

Subject: Re: Weekly leadership signalcheck — QBR readiness, OKR highlights, immediate asks

Soojin —

I dug into the staging traces this morning. Initial read: the p95 regression correlates with a change in the batching window plus a background process that primes KV entries less aggressively for long prefixes. Two quick items: 

1) Can you drop the perf dashboard link and the specific sample lines into the tracker (INF-9823)? I want the exact trace IDs for the dry-run.
2) Short-term mitigation: we can flip a routing flag to keep long-sequence requests on the previous batching heuristic. That is low-risk and reversible. I estimate a 30–60 minute ops-rollback window once approved.

If the execs want a safe approach for the QBR deck, propose we commit to the routing-flag mitigation and include a plan to harden the KV priming in Q1. I'll add a brief slide note.

On the attachments: I see the latency CSV; it would help if you add a small sample of the raw request/response times (first 50 rows) inline in the ticket.

-Markus

- Markus: adding the perf-dashboard snapshot and the first 50 lines of raw traces to INF-9823 now. I'll tag you when it's ready. Rolling the routing flag is my recommended default for the dry-run; I'll coordinate the change and the rollback window.
- Laura: noted on the finance assumptions. I've added an assumptions appendix to the Drive slide and called out the cost-reduction math.
- Vivek: Finance + Sales alignment required for credits. Vivek, can you loop Kelly and Bryan and advise here? We'll hold the credit ask until we have their nod.
- Tessa/Jonas: I'll post a one-page runbook (2 escalation examples + owner contact list) to the Drive by 4pm PT.

Action summary (short):
- INF-9823: traces + dashboard (Markus/Soojin) — ETA 1:30pm PT
- Drive slide + assumptions (Soojin/Laura) — ETA noon PT (comments from Laura noted)
- Runbook one-pager (Tessa/Jonas/Soojin) — ETA 4pm PT
- Credits: Vivek to align with Finance (no decision until confirmation)

I'll update the exec dry-run deck after the 1:30pm trace update and ping for the 3:30pm quick sync if needed.
